### Recommendation

Your best choice comes down to **Deductible Traditional** versus **Direct Roth**; a **Backdoor Roth should be avoided right now**.

Because you hold a **$22,400 Vanguard Traditional IRA**, attempting a backdoor Roth conversion triggers the IRS **pro-rata rule** (Form 8606). Under this rule, the IRS aggregates all your pre-tax IRA balances on December 31, making the vast majority of any backdoor conversion taxable as ordinary income.

---

### How each option works for your situation

#### 1. Deductible Traditional IRA (Strongest for current-year tax & health insurance)
- **Full deductibility**: Because you are self-employed with no workplace retirement plan, your Traditional IRA contributions are **100% tax-deductible**, regardless of your income level (up to the 2026 limit of **$7,500**).
- **Marketplace subsidy synergy**: Traditional contributions reduce your Adjusted Gross Income (AGI / MAGI) dollar-for-dollar. For self-employed individuals buying health coverage through the marketplace, lowering your MAGI can increase your **Premium Tax Credit (PTC)** and lower your monthly health insurance premiums.
- **Self-employment tax note**: Traditional IRA deductions reduce federal income tax, but they do not reduce Schedule SE self-employment tax.

#### 2. Direct Roth IRA (Best for tax-free retirement growth)
- **No backdoor needed if under income limits**: In 2026, the Roth IRA phase-out range for single filers is **$153,000 to $168,000 MAGI**. If your net income is below $153,000, you can contribute directly to a Roth IRA with zero conversion steps and zero pro-rata complications.
- **Benefits**: Your contributions grow completely tax-free, withdrawals in retirement are tax-free with no Required Minimum Distributions (RMDs), and original contributions can be withdrawn penalty-free at any time.

#### 3. Backdoor Roth IRA (Blocked by pro-rata rule unless restructured)
- **The problem**: If your MAGI exceeds $168,000 and you want Roth dollars, you cannot do a clean backdoor conversion while holding the $22,400 Vanguard Traditional IRA balance.
- **The fix**: If you want to use the backdoor Roth in the future, you would first need to establish a **Solo 401(k)** that accepts incoming rollovers, roll the entire $22,400 pre-tax balance into the Solo 401(k) before December 31, and then complete the backdoor Roth once your Traditional IRA balance is $0.

---

### How to decide your next step

- **Choose Deductible Traditional ($7,500 for 2026)** if you want immediate tax savings at your federal marginal rate and want to lower your MAGI to optimize ACA marketplace health insurance subsidies.
- **Choose Direct Roth ($7,500 for 2026)** if your MAGI is under $153,000 and you prefer tax-free compounding in retirement over an immediate tax deduction.
